rationale.conceptual: Implementing a linked-cluster expansion up to ninth order for a kagome-lattice spin Hamiltonian requires deep understanding of many-body perturbation theory, cluster topology, and the translation of involved analytic expressions into robust numerical code; multiple interacting components (Hilbert space decomposition, effective Hamiltonian matrix series, LSW normalization) make this a challenging implementation.
rationale.execution: The pipeline involves several sequential stages (cluster expansion, LSW series, ratio computation, CSV writing) but is entirely code-only with standard libraries; no external data assembly or fragile tool orchestration, placing it at a moderate orchestration complexity.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires implementing a ninth-order linked-cluster expansion (IEP) on a kagome lattice, including Holstein-Primakoff linear spin wave calculations, series ratio formation, and dispersion output. The method is non-trivial, involving perturbation theory, cluster topology, and matrix derivation; the pipeline is multi-step but self-contained. No GPU or large data; RAM ~2-4 GB.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The expansion generates a moderate set of coefficients (clusters up to 9 links/10 sites) and diagonalization is for 3x3 matrices repeatedly across k-points; the entire computation fits within a few GB of RAM and is strictly CPU-bound.
